selection: Predeclared source random frames and roles; pretrained model boundary proposals plus fixed raw-gradient refinement; every selected fixed-camera frame is retained or explicitly excluded.
limitations: Mat dimensions and corner-axis assignment are conditional operator/config inputs.
Centered principal point, square pixels and zero distortion constrain the baseline; free intrinsic models expose remaining gauges.
All camera poses are in the mat frame. Named physical static CAD correspondence is needed to register the robot base.
Repeated static views do not create calibration-board motion or establish absolute metric accuracy.
conclusion: Model-derived fresh source pixels yield conditional camera estimates, but neither shared camera/mat pose passes every whole-frame verification at the declared3px scale. No physical geometry accepted or adopted. Failures may reflect segmentation/occlusion, mat motion, camera changes or restrictive intrinsics; these data do not uniquely identify the cause.
extraction_revision_note: First proposal used a convex-hull corner and failed occluded frames. Training-fit frame26 led to orientation-constrained edge consensus. Training-fit frame0 exposed a longer gripper occlusion cut; the final top proposal uses the model boundary upper envelope. Final rules frozen before final verification projection scores. Earlier exploratory outputs remain local evidence.

fixed_foot_contour_check.method: Project the exact pinned CAD top triangles and, separately, all lower-foot triangles including sidewalls for each previously declared wing/XY/yaw basin through the new conditional mat camera. Compare every model-mask external component with uncapped bidirectional nearest-contour errors; report IoU separately. No frame pixels refit a base pose.
limitations: SAM-visible foot material is not an independently registered CAD identity.
Nominal top-plane projection omits visible side thickness. The separate solid-lower-foot projection includes sides but both omit holder/arm/clamp occlusion and print/CAD mismatch.
Mat camera and mat/base height remain conditional assumptions. A better contour score cannot grant physical calibration or joint-zero acceptance.
Prior candidate basins came from an earlier explored training foot image. New capture scores can reject inconsistency but do not turn ambiguous matches into metrology.

verification_scope: Whole-frame verification pixels never enter camera parameter optimization or numeric solution selection. Earlier exploratory verification scores were inspected during debugging; final extraction revisions were motivated by training-fit frame0/26. This is development verification, not a pristine untouched acceptance set.
